data.body:
Researchers who follow children through primary school keep finding the same thing: those who get personal mail ask more questions about the world.

## Why mail works

A letter is addressed to one child. It feels like a secret, and children read secrets slowly and carefully.

In every letter there is one tiny hidden thing to find: a snail, a kite, a cup of cocoa.

A single letter takes about three evenings. First the pencil sketch, then the washes, then the tiny details that children find and point at.

## Why not print from a screen?

Because a child can tell. Real paint has a little wobble, and that wobble says a person was here.

## Post it together

Walk to the postbox the same day. The little thud as the letter drops in is half the magic.

- Write on the same day every week
- Keep stamps in a jar by the door
- Read the reply out loud as a family

> A letter is a small promise that someone is thinking of you.

data.body:
The hardest part of a letter is the blank page. Ask for one sentence, not one page. "Tell Pip what you had for breakfast" is a complete letter, and a proud one.

## Make the tools theirs

Let your child pick the paper, the pen and the stickers. A letter written with a glitter pen is worth ten typed ones.
